text:
jess: Heads-up: we hit two weird failures in staging when pulling the JS SDK from our pnpm monorepo into a Cloudflare Worker build. 1) the worker bundle couldn't resolve @redwood/sdk at runtime, 2) our editor complained about missing types. Both worked OK when installing the published tarball.

omar: Did you check the package exports + package.json in dist? pnpm symlinks can expose the source package.json, not the published one.

jess: Here's the SDK package.json we use in repo root (simplified):
```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","main":"dist/index.js","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.js"}}
```
Editor error: "No declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'" even though dist/index.d.ts exists after build. Worker bundler: "Error: Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk'" during runtime.

li: Quick checklist: pnpm creates symlinks in node_modules/.pnpm/.., many bundlers treat symlinked packages as external by default. What's your esbuild/webpack rollup config?

jess: esbuild via our deploy pipeline. We had default `preserveSymlinks: true` set via Node's default. When I toggled to false, bundler included package files but TS still preferred workspace root types.

omar: Two practical fixes we've used: (A) copy a minimal package.json into dist on build (postbuild cp package.json dist/package.json) so bundler resolves the same manifest as published, (B) add a typesVersions map to help tsserver prefer dist types in a workspace.

li: For completeness, sample typesVersions we used:
```json
"typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/*"]}}
```
It's a bit hacky but works across VSCode/tsserver.

jess: Trying that now. Also discovered that our SDK's exports didn't include a `types` condition — adding it probably helps editors that consume exports conditions.

omar: Example exports with types:
```json
"exports": {
  "import": {"default":"./dist/index.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"},
  "require": {"default":"./dist/index.js","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}
}
```
Note: not all tools honor `types` in exports, but npm pack + published packages behave consistently.

jess: Good tip. After adding dist/package.json and typesVersions, editor errors go away locally. But deploying to CF still failed intermittently. Digging logs showed the worker bundle sometimes omitted the Authorization header when our SDK retried requests. Error surface: 401 on retry or missing header. Works without ESM build.

ryan: That sounds like a fetch cloning bug we hit: retries that reuse Request objects can lose ephemeral headers if the SDK uses `request.clone()` and then serializes in a way not supported by the worker runtime. What retry lib/version are you using?

jess: We used an internal helper that wraps fetch with retry logic and reuses Request objects. The wrapper does `const r = req.clone()` and then uses `fetch(r)`. In Node dev it worked; in worker runtime, clone() seemed to drop Authorization intermittently.

li: Worker runtimes may implement Headers differently (proxy-backed). Safer approach: when you retry, create a fresh Request copying headers explicitly:
```js
const copy = new Request(req.url, {
  method: req.method,
  headers: new Headers(req.headers),
  body: req.body,
});
await fetch(copy);
```
This ensures Authorization isn't lost. Also ensure you don't stringify the Request body and then reuse the same stream without buffering.

omar: Another gotcha: if you use a small retry delay and the Request body is a stream (read-once), the second attempt will have no body. For JSON bodies, prefer serializing into a Buffer/string up-front so retries can re-send reliably.

jess: Oof we were streaming in dev but not buffering. Changed to buffer JSON bodies before sending and switched clone -> explicit copy. Staging now shows headers preserved.

ryan: For the monorepo resolution side, we also added a CI test that builds a small example workspace (pnpm workspace with a minimal app) and runs the builder for CF/Vercel to catch these symlink/exports issues early. Saved us multiple regressions.

jess: Love that. I'll add a minimal example + CI step in the SDK repo. Will include: postbuild cp of package.json into dist, exports+types in package.json, typesVersions fallback, esbuild config note (preserveSymlinks: false), and retry clone example.

omar: Also leave a note for yarn users — hoisting differs: yarn classic hoists more aggressively, and yarn berry PnP is another beast. Suggest separate docs for pnpm vs yarn.

ci-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/501 for examples + CI check and added labels: docs, ci.

jess: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1012 — contains examples/monorepo, docs/monorepo.md, and a small unit test for the retry helper.

li: Nice. TL;DR for folks: if you're using pnpm workspaces + edge runtimes -> (1) ensure bundler resolves symlinked packages (preserveSymlinks: false), (2) include a dist/package.json during local dev to match published layout, (3) add exports types and optionally typesVersions to help TS, (4) buffer request bodies for retries and copy headers explicitly in worker runtimes.

jess: Thanks everyone! Leaving the PR link and CI issue here in case others run into it. :sparkles:
